messages:
maria: Heads-up — I found a set of customer sessions where streaming + toolcall + client-side truncation ended up double-counting ~30-40 tokens on the ledger. Example log: `ledger: sess=abc123 path=stream/toolcall tokens=+120 provisional=true` then later `ledger: sess=abc123 path=stream tokens=+35 confirmed=true` — seems like the suffix trim created a provisional toolcall credit that never reconciled when the stream truncated.
vikram: Hmm. Is that the case where the client sends a `stop_stream` mid-toolcall and the toolcall completion arrived after the stream EOF?
jess: Yep, saw similar in telemetry last week. The provisional vs confirmed flow is fragile around out-of-order ACKs.
maria: My quick repro: start stream, trigger toolcall, client disconnects before toolcall final chunk, server marks provisional toolcall credit, stream truncates, reconnect resumes as a plain stream and confirms additional token delta. Ledger sees both.
kevin: Can you paste the minimal trace? we need to see event ordering.
maria: trace (sanitized):
```
1716067890 EVENT stream.start sess=abc123
1716067891 EVENT toolcall.start sess=abc123 call_id=c1
1716067893 EVENT toolcall.provisional_credit sess=abc123 +80 provisional=true
1716067894 EVENT stream.truncate sess=abc123 client_stop=true
1716067896 EVENT stream.resume sess=abc123
1716067898 EVENT toolcall.final sess=abc123 call_id=c1 +20 confirmed=true
```
Ledger events: provisional +80 then confirmed +20, and resume added +35 for resumed tokens.
louise: So provisional credit not being reconciled downward when the final toolcall confirms with fewer tokens. We should be diffing provisional vs confirmed and only apply the delta.
vikram: Agreed. Current implementation treats provisional as immediate minting and confirmed as an additional commit rather than reconciliation.
jess: Fix idea: introduce a reconciliation delta step when toolcall confirms — replace provisional event with confirmed instead of adding. E.g. `ledger.reconcile(sess, call_id, confirmed_tokens)` which subtracts provisional and adds confirmed.
kevin: That helps, but we also need to handle the case where stream truncation deletes some streamed tokens (prefix capture) and auto-resume generates a new provisional for the resumed tail. Reconcile needs to be idempotent and based on call_id.
maria: Also UI impact: console currently shows provisional credits as "unsettled usage" which customers see as spikes. We should surface reconciliations in the usage timeline as a single net adjustment, not two separate positive spikes.
louise: Suggestion: add an `adjustment` event type with `net_delta` so the time series plotting can apply a negative point when provisional is reduced. Keeps the chart sane.
jess: Telemetry: add trace_id to every provisional/confirm event and an `origin` tag (stream|resume|reconnect) so we can query by root cause.
ops-bot: deploy-checklist: run canary with reconciliation flag off-by-default, gather 72h of provisional->confirmed churn metrics.
vikram: Implementation plan: 1) Server: change provisional commit to be tombstoned on confirm and emit `reconcile` with net_delta. 2) Ledger: support idempotent reconcile by call_id. 3) Console: display `adjustment` points and expose reconciliations in usage API. 4) Telemetry: add trace_id/origin.
kevin: Edge case: what if provisional is never confirmed (client permanently disconnects)? Current behavior is to eventually expire provisional after TTL and mark refunded. Keep that TTL but ensure expiration produces an `adjustment` with negative delta.
maria: Testing: add unit for out-of-order events + e2e with simulated flaky client rejoin. Also craft a query to find affected customers in last 30d: `select ledger where provisional=true and not reconciled older than 48h`.
louise: UX: In the console billing view, show a small hover tooltip "Includes provisional credits that may be adjusted" and add a reconciliations tab for enterprise accounts.
jess: One more thought — routing interaction: when fallback routes trigger a model-swap mid-toolcall, we can get two distinct call_ids for same logical intent. Need an upstream coalescing key (session_intent_id) so reconcile knows which provisional maps to which confirm across route hops.\ev: wait who is ev? (ignore)
kevin: Good catch — we'll need to propagate `intent_id` in routing headers. Add to internal API contract.
maria: Timeline: Vikram + Kevin take infra changes; Jess + Louise do console/telemetry. Ops will run canary. I'll open a PR with spec + sample trace.
jess: :thumbsup: will add dashboards for provisional churn.
louise: I'll draft console tooltip copy and reconciliation toggle.
vikram: I'll add ledger migration for reconcile index on call_id + intent_id.
kevin: Plan to canary next Monday, rollback-able via feature flag.
maria: Thanks — created issue #INF-1429 with links to traces and the proposed schema.
ops-bot: note: incident-guardrail: if canary shows >0.5% net-charge-delta on reserved accounts, auto-disable reconcile and alert billing-team.
kevin: Sounds good. Any objections to soft-trim naming? I used "reconcile-on-confirm" internally but "soft-trim" is clearer to product.
jess: Prefer "reconcile-on-confirm" for code, soft-trim for docs.
maria: Cool. Owners assigned. I'll post PR link when ready.
